messages:
lina_chen: Quick sync — proposing 'priority classes' for per-route limits so SLA tiers map directly to billing tiers. Sketch below; want ops + billing input before I file a formal RFC.

samir_kapoor: +1. High level: are we talking hard quota enforcement per-route, or soft limits that surface warnings and then throttle per-account?

lina_chen: Thinking hybrid: hard monthly quotas for cost-control, soft realtime rate buckets for latency-sensitive routes (with automatic fallback to cheaper model).

maria_g: Important: token accounting differs by surface. Chat = prompt+response tokens, embeddings = input tokens only, rerank = input + per-candidate overhead. Need explicit billed_token field so billing and telemetry align.

samir_kapoor: Agreed. Draft mapping for API events: 
```json
{
  "usage": {
    "input_tokens": 123,
    "output_tokens": 456,
    "billed_tokens": 579,
    "billing_dimension": "billed_tokens"
  }
}
```
Use billed_tokens for quota checks/invoicing.

tom_bradley: Customer ask: enterprise wants per-route hard-limits + per-customer soft-limits (to protect against noisy tenants). How do priority classes interact with per-customer reserved capacity?

lina_chen: Priority classes should be orthogonal: route -> route_tier (gold/silver/baseline), customer -> account_tier. Enforcement rules evaluate (route_tier, account_tier, reserved_capacity) in that order. If reserved capacity exists, honor it first, then route hard quota, then account soft-limit.

eva_product: We also need an SRE escape hatch: emergency override that disables per-route throttles for given trace IDs for debugging, with auditlog and 2-person approval.

maria_g: Launch criteria proposal: (1) per-route enforcement implemented in runtime + unit tests, (2) integration test showing correct billed_tokens for chat/embeddings/rerank, (3) billing mapping exported to invoices, (4) canary with 5% of traffic for two weeks, (5) docs and migration guide.

samir_kapoor: Technical note on batching: when we batch N requests for continuous batching, billed_tokens must be summed per logical request before applying quotas. Do not double-count shared KV cache hits.

lina_chen: Good catch. Add rule: prefix/KV cache savings reduce billed_tokens for subsequent requests; quotas deduct actual billed_tokens after cache deduction.

samir_kapoor: Enforcement pseudocode idea: 
```text
on_request(req):
  billed = compute_billed_tokens(req)
  if route_hard_quota.remaining < billed: reject(429 + "quota_exceeded")
  elif account_soft_bucket.available < billed: apply_early_throttle()
  else: accept_and_deduct(billed)
```
We should simulate this in load tests.

tom_bradley: Billing asks: we need a stable field name customers can rely on for chargebacks. Proposal: export "billed_tokens" in /usage events and invoices. No internal renaming without 6mo deprecation.

maria_g: +1 to stable field. Also include per-route "billing_dimension" metadata so marketplace partners can map to custom billing.

lina_chen: Ops concerns: per-route limit table size could blow up — we should support route tagging and inheritance (wildcard routes inherit parent limits). Also TTL for route overrides.

eva_product: Can we add an audit column to the route metadata: last_changed_by, change_reason, change_ts — required for enterprise compliance.

samir_kapoor: I'll add a schema snippet for route metadata: 
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/chat",
  "route_tier": "gold",
  "rate_limit": { "per_minute": 6000, "burst": 1200 },
  "quota": { "monthly_billed_tokens": 10000000 },
  "billing_dimension": "billed_tokens",
  "inherit_from": "/v1/*",
  "audit": { "last_changed_by": "maria_g", "change_ts": "2026-03-24T10:00:00Z" }
}
```

lina_chen: Decision runway: collect feedback by EOD Friday, then Tom drafts RFC next week.

tom_bradley: Action items: I will draft the API contract for route metadata + migration path.

samir_kapoor: I'll add enforcement sim to k8s loadtest job and verify batch/cache accounting.

maria_g: I'll prepare billing mapping doc and invoice sample for finance to review.

eva_product: I'll add the compliance/audit requirements to the RFC checklist.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline started: perf/load-test-suite #421 queued (links: https://ci.redwood.local/job/421). :rocket:

lina_chen: Thanks everyone — will shepherd RFC and lock stakeholder review. :thumbsup:
